expected_behavior: within the canonical isolated regression path, native cardiac output falls as PEEP rises across the graded probe
within the canonical isolated regression path, MAP falls as PEEP rises across the graded probe
measured CVP rises as PEEP rises across the canonical graded probe
total blood volume and blood-volume fraction do not change merely because PEEP changed
static PEEP does not create a large artificial hypocapnia response
the intrathoracic-relative preload proxy falls as PEEP rises across the canonical graded probe
at fixed VA-ECMO controls in the canonical coupled regression probe, patient-directed ECMO flow falls as PEEP rises even though measured CVP rises
interpretive_guardrail: a higher measured CVP during positive airway pressure is not evidence that intravascular volume or effective drainage preload increased; Phase 10a uses the explicitly derived intrathoracic-relative preload proxy for ECMO drainage, and its quantitative PEEP-to-flow magnitude remains an educational regression behavior rather than a validated bedside prediction
recovery_model: return AirwayPort.peep_cmh2o to baseline and re-equilibrate the same patient
recovery_scope: deterministic cardiopulmonary re-equilibration after control reversal; not a history-dependent recruitment/derecruitment recovery test
not_modeled: advanced ventilator modes beyond the implemented pressure-control pathway
a validated patient/device-specific transmural central venous pressure measurement
a clinically validated quantitative PEEP-to-ECMO-drainage dose-response
future_retest_conditions: advanced ventilator modes or synchrony mechanisms materially change mean-airway-pressure/hemodynamic behavior
dynamic recruitment/derecruitment or lung injury state is introduced
the Phase 10a intrathoracic-relative preload proxy is replaced by a more physiologically explicit venous/transmural model
cannula-collapse or intrathoracic drainage mechanics are materially expanded
notes: PEEP values are regression stimuli, not a neonatal ventilator prescription.
Phase 2d implemented learner-operable pressure-control ventilation (PIP/PEEP/rate/Ti/FiO2); CBC07 remains specifically a PEEP/hemodynamic contract rather than a full ventilator-validation contract.

External pediatric/neonatal evidence shows the hemodynamic response to PEEP is heterogeneous and often modest; the monotonic CO/MAP response is retained as the simulator canonical isolated regression path, not a universal clinical prediction.

Phase 10a migrates the ECMO drainage boundary from measured CVP to the Phase 9a intrathoracic-relative preload proxy; measured CVP remains independently displayed and authoritative as a measured pressure.
The coupled drainage direction is now protected as a bounded/reversible simulator teaching behavior; exact magnitude is not clinically validated.

evidence_scope.supported: positive airway pressure can alter venous return/right-heart loading and can reduce cardiac output; measured CVP can rise with increased intrathoracic pressure
evidence_scope.not_supported_as_universal: a fixed or necessarily clinically important fall in cardiac output or MAP at each PEEP increment in every ventilated neonate/child
evidence_scope.status: external evidence packet complete; expert sign-off pending
